claims: A strict overhead press must declare base, laterality, implement quantity, rack, grip, no-leg-drive policy, full repetition cycle, range, tempo, and equipment operations.
Standing, seated, tall-kneeling, and half-kneeling bases materially change balance, trunk demand, setup, and failure response; they cannot share one selectable source contract.
Implement stability changes overhead-press demand and must be represented explicitly.
The controlled contract declares standing base, two kettlebells, bilateral press, rack, handle orientation, free-bell path, no deliberate leg drive, owned range, controlled return, and reset.
Overhead pressing involves deltoid, triceps, trapezius, scapular, rotator-cuff, grip, and trunk contributions that depend on configuration.
Exact cards declare shoulder, scapulothoracic, elbow, wrist, thoracic, lumbar, pelvic, hip, knee, ankle, and foot roles without claiming isolated activation.
A less stable implement changes muscle activity during overhead pressing.
Two independently moving kettlebells require a declared rack, handle and bell position, bilateral path, owned finish, controlled return, and safe clean or assisted setup.
Implement stability and independent paths contribute to exercise demand.
Score exercise complexity and physical difficulty only, derive overall as their maximum, and keep athlete skill or proficiency out of exercise cards.
Controlled eccentric tempo influences internal load and short-term recovery.
Track load per kettlebell, combined load, repetitions, range, tempo, effort, set duration, grip and rack fatigue, local symptoms, and next-day response.
Resistance training requires inspected equipment, stable setup, adequate clearance, controlled progression, and appropriate supervision.
Require two matched intact kettlebells, level non-slip footing, overhead clearance, a clear clean and set-down zone, and a declared spot or failed-repetition plan.
Resistance dose depends on sets, repetitions, load, effort, rest, order, and progression.
Use quality repetitions with enough rest to preserve standing base, rack, independent paths, owned range, and secure set-down.
Instruction establishes equipment, setup, start, action, breathing, return, and safe finish.
Cue a safe clean or assisted rack, stable feet, stacked ribs and pelvis, strict press without a dip, controlled independent paths, owned finish, return to rack, and secure set-down.
Qualified supervision, manageable resistance, correct technique, and gradual progression are central resistance-training safeguards.
Stop for pain, instability, numbness, dizziness, pressure symptoms, grip loss, bell collision, unsafe clean or set-down, balance loss, rib flare, asymmetric path, range loss, or grinding.
Exercise order, load, volume, frequency, and progression should match the intended adaptation.
Place demanding bilateral kettlebell pressing before fatigue-sensitive overhead skills or dense pressing and count it toward shoulder, triceps, grip, trunk, and recovery budgets.
Athletes need a plain-language setup, action, finish, self-check, and symptom escalation rule.
Expose kettlebell count and mass, rack, base, range, tempo, repetitions, rest, expected effort, safe clean or handoff, and set-down before the set.
Implement stability changes the overhead-press task.
Observe footing, clean or handoff, rack, handle and bell position, grip, wrist-elbow stack, scapular motion, rib-pelvis position, independent paths, symmetry, range, tempo, effort, and secure finish.
Resistance training should be individualized to readiness, body size, equipment fit, technical control, and supervision.

Options include lighter matched kettlebells, fewer repetitions, shorter owned range, longer rest, dumbbell or seated substitution after review, and text, still-image, audio, tactile, or live instruction.
Two-kettlebell standing execution is an implement variant of the bilateral standing strict press.

Changing to one arm, kneeling, seated, push press, bottom-up, alternating, or assisted eccentric-only execution changes laterality, base, stability, ordered action, or primary constraint and requires separate review.
YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com.

Retained candidates returned current oEmbed metadata and iframe markup on 2026-08-01, but title metadata cannot establish exact base, rack, handle orientation, range, tempo, safety, captions, accessibility, quality, reviewer, or approval.

assessmentSummary.identity: A bilateral standing free-weight strict overhead press; the new exact kettlebell variant uses two matched kettlebells in a declared bilateral front rack, no deliberate leg drive, independent controlled paths, an owned overhead finish, and return to the same rack.
currentCardFindings: Version 2 already completes barbell, dumbbell, sandbag, and dumbbell-tempo variants.
The newly exposed Kettlebell Strict Press card cannot be consolidated wholesale because its source permits a stance or kneeling base and does not consistently declare one versus two kettlebells.

The explicit Double Kettlebell source supports implement quantity and bilateral action but still does not fix base; the canonical standing variant is a new review-state authoring, not a claimed source mapping.
Five refreshed candidates cover barbell, dumbbell, sandbag, and two double-kettlebell title matches; all exact-match and approval fields remain unset.
